about: Iowa grant programs with their own application windows that aren't posted on IowaGrants.gov, entered by hand from each program's own page: Humanities Iowa's Mini Grants, the Iowa Arts Council's SlideRoom grants, the State Historical Society of Iowa's Historical Resource Development Program, and the Attorney General's opioid settlement and victim services grants. grantmatch/local.py checks this file and turns each entry into an Iowa program record; the weekly page watcher rereads every page. Change an entry only from the official page, and update its checked date.

programs.title: Humanities Iowa Mini Grants
programs.objectives: Small grants for public humanities projects in Iowa that don't fit Humanities Iowa's other programs, such as talks, discussions, exhibits and local history events for out-of-school adults.
programs.who: Iowa nonprofit organizations serving the out-of-school adult public. The project must engage the humanities and fit Humanities Iowa's mission.
programs.application: Apply on Humanities Iowa's Submittable page (humanitiesiowa.submittable.com). Staff encourage a call or email before you apply. No application fee.
programs.award: Up to $3,000. A 1:1 cash or in-kind match is required.
programs.deadlines: Rolling. Decisions take about 6 to 8 weeks, so apply at least six weeks before the project starts.
programs.contact: Humanities Iowa, info@humanitiesiowa.org, PO Box 881, Ames, IA 50010
programs.subjects: Humanities; History; Public programs; Adult education; Culture

programs.title: Art Project Grant for Organizations
programs.agency: Iowa Arts Council (Iowa Economic Development Authority)
programs.objectives: One-time arts projects that give Iowans an arts experience or arts learning opportunity: events, performances, exhibitions, festivals, workshops and public art with community engagement.
programs.who: Active Iowa nonprofits registered with the Iowa Secretary of State, with 501(c)(3) status and a staffed office in Iowa; border-city nonprofits serving Iowa audiences; schools and educational institutions; and local, county, state or tribal governments in Iowa. Individuals and businesses can't apply.
programs.application: Apply through the Iowa Arts Council's SlideRoom portal (iowaartscouncil.slideroom.com), not IowaGrants. Read that year's guidelines first.
programs.award: FY27: $5,000 to $25,000, with a 1:1 match of the amount requested.
programs.deadlines: Once a year. The FY27 deadline was April 1, 2026 at 11:59 p.m. for projects July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2027. Watch the page for the FY28 round.
programs.contact: Laura Hayes, Arts Grant Manager, Iowa Arts Council, 515-348-6327
programs.subjects: Arts; Culture; Performing arts; Visual arts; Public art; Arts education

programs.title: Cultural Capacity Building Grant
programs.agency: Iowa Arts Council (Iowa Economic Development Authority)
programs.objectives: General operating support over three years for Iowa arts, cultural and humanities organizations working on their cultural and managerial excellence and community service.
programs.who: Iowa arts, cultural and humanities nonprofits with annual cash operating expenses above $10,000. Organizations already holding another Iowa Arts Council grant for the same year may be ineligible; see the guidelines.
programs.application: Read the guidelines and schedule a meeting with the program manager through the program page; applications go through the Iowa Arts Council's SlideRoom portal when a round opens.
programs.award: Multi-year general operating support; the amount is set in each round's guidelines.
programs.deadlines: Opens once every three years. Not accepting applications when checked. Watch the page for the next three-year round.
programs.contact: Jennie Knoebel, Director, Iowa Arts Council, 515-348-6324
programs.subjects: Arts; Culture; Humanities; General operating support; Capacity building

programs.title: Historical Resource Development Program (HRDP)
programs.agency: State Historical Society of Iowa (Iowa Department of Administrative Services)
programs.objectives: Grants to preserve, conserve, interpret, enhance and teach the public about Iowa's historical resources, in three categories: documentary collections, historic preservation and museums. Funded by REAP.
programs.who: Nonprofits, governments, tribes, individuals and for-profits, for a historical resource located in Iowa.
programs.application: Read the general guidelines, your category's instructions and its scoring rubric, then apply through the program's SlideRoom link. Emergency HRDP has its own guidelines and application.
programs.award: Up to $50,000, with a required match; match ratios vary by category and applicant.
programs.deadlines: Once a year. The 2026 deadline was May 1, 2026, for projects July 1, 2026 to November 30, 2028. Emergency HRDP (documentary collections only) opens each July 1 and is first come, first served while funds last. Watch the page for the 2027 round.
programs.contact: State Historical Society of Iowa grants staff, history.iowa.gov/contact
programs.subjects: History; Historic preservation; Museums; Archives; Collections

programs.title: Opioid Settlement Grants
programs.agency: Iowa Attorney General (Iowa Department of Justice)
programs.objectives: Programs, services and initiatives that respond to the opioid crisis in Iowa, paid from the Attorney General's 25% share of Iowa's opioid settlement money. Projects must fit the national opioid settlements' core strategies and approved uses and the Iowa Opioid Allocation Memorandum of Understanding.
programs.who: Organizations with an eligible opioid abatement project. The office encourages projects of all sizes and scopes.
programs.application: Apply in the Iowa Department of Justice grants system (iowadoj.intelligrants.com). The funding page links the application and instructions for creating a new user for the opioid grant.
programs.award: About $20 million is expected to be available through June 30, 2030. No per-award limit is stated.
programs.deadlines: Open; applications are reviewed on a rolling basis.
programs.subjects: Opioids; Substance use; Prevention; Harm reduction; Treatment; Recovery

programs.title: Victim Services Competitive Grants
programs.agency: Iowa Attorney General, Victim Assistance Section
programs.objectives: Multi-year funding for victim services in Iowa, awarded by region: sexual abuse and rape crisis centers, domestic abuse programs and shelters, services for survivors of homicide and other violent crime, culturally specific programs and statewide hotlines. Separate competitive rounds cover training and technical assistance and criminal justice projects.
programs.who: Agencies that provide victim services, justice support to crime victims, training, community education, crime prevention, or technical assistance to victim service providers. See Iowa Administrative Code 61-9 for the full rules.
programs.application: Watch for the notice of funding opportunity and application webinar on the funding page. Applications go through the Iowa Department of Justice grants system.
programs.award: Set in each round's notice of funding opportunity.
programs.deadlines: Awarded on a multi-year cycle. The current round is closed; the office expects the next victim services round to start around January 2029, with an application webinar.
programs.contact: Iowa Attorney General, Victim Assistance Section, Hoover Building, 1305 E Walnut St, Des Moines, IA 50319
programs.subjects: Crime victims; Victim services; Domestic violence; Sexual assault; Homicide survivors
